findings.issue: Block 37 says assai 'sounds slightly more emphatic' than molto (i.e. stronger), but block 53 says scholars argue assai can mean 'rather' (slightly SOFTER than 'very'). The two blocks make opposite claims about the same word.
findings.evidence: #37: 'it is close in meaning to molto, but sounds slightly more emphatic in Italian'  vs  #53: 'some scholars argue *assai* can mean "rather" (slightly softer than "very")'
findings.fix: Reconcile the two: either drop the 'slightly more emphatic' claim in block 37 and simply say assai is interchangeable with molto ('very'), matching block 53, or remove the contradictory nuance in one of the blocks.

findings.issue: Fully re-explains the crescendo hairpin and the meaning of mf (mezzo forte) from scratch, including pronunciation. Dynamics and hairpin markings were already taught in L1#12; an applied 'putting it all together' step should recap briefly, not re-teach the definitions.
findings.evidence: "A **crescendo** (creh-SHEN-doe) means gradually getting louder. The hairpin shows you exactly where the grow starts and where it finishes." ... "**mf** stands for *mezzo forte*, which means moderately loud."
findings.fix: Trim to a one-line recap, e.g. "As you learned earlier, a crescendo hairpin means grow gradually louder, arriving at mf (mezzo forte, moderately loud) by bar 4."

findings.issue: The accent mark was already taught in L1#12 ('Accent and Sforzando'). This block re-explains its full definition (symbol, meaning, physical execution) rather than briefly recapping, despite the 'quick reminder' heading.
findings.evidence: "the **accent mark**, the greater-than symbol **>** placed above or below a note head. It means: play that note louder and with more attack... Drop the weight of your arm into the key for that one moment, then relax immediately."
findings.fix: Trim to a one-line recap (e.g. 'As you learned earlier, the accent > means play that note louder with more attack') and drop the re-explanation of technique.

findings.issue: Content-free framing sentence dressed as teaching; restates the obvious and instructs the reader to 'read carefully' rather than adding information.
findings.evidence: "Character terms are instructions for your body as much as your ears. ... Read the physical description carefully for each term below."
findings.fix: Cut or reduce to a single lead-in sentence.

findings.issue: Invented 'feel' analogy that is confusing and adds no real technical content (pressing a bruise is something one avoids, not a model of gentle touch).
findings.evidence: "Imagine you are pressing the key as gently as you would press a bruise."
findings.fix: Cut this sentence; the preceding instructions (reduce weight, loose low wrist) already convey a gentle touch.

findings.issue: Motivational padding with no instructional content.
findings.evidence: "There is no single right answer. Trust your instinct."
findings.fix: Trim to a brief factual note that espressivo allows personal interpretation, or cut.

findings.issue: Subjective padding claim that adds no teaching content and cannot be substantiated.
findings.evidence: "This is perhaps the most precise physical instruction of all the character terms."
findings.fix: Cut the sentence; go straight to describing the leggiero touch.

findings.issue: The crescendo is coded as a literal text annotation "<" rather than an ABC crescendo hairpin decoration, so it will render as the character < above the stave instead of a proper crescendo hairpin.
findings.fix: Use a real hairpin, e.g. !crescendo(! ... !crescendo)! (or !<(! !<)!), so the marking prints as a crescendo hairpin the caption and later Step 4 refer to.

findings.issue: Vague 'feel' padding dressed up as instruction.
findings.evidence: "This kind of gentle slowing at the end of a phrase or piece is one of the most natural and expressive things a musician can do. It feels like a breath before silence."
findings.fix: Delete these two sentences; the preceding definition of poco rit. is sufficient.

findings.issue: Motivational padding with no new teaching content; purple prose ('the composer's voice, speaking to you across time') that adds nothing a student can act on.
findings.evidence: "Learning this vocabulary is one of the most rewarding steps in your musical journey. The notes on the page are only part of the picture. These terms and signs are the composer's voice, speaking to you across time..."
findings.fix: Cut this block, or reduce to a single practical sentence.
